I have to stop it and then redirect it with `/to-prd`.
So I added this to the end of the `/grill-me` skill:

Once you have no more questions, DO NOT START IMPLEMENTATION without user permission, instead DO prompt the user for a next step.

items.author: itsfordanny
items.body:
## Problem

`/grill-me` produces excellent structured decisions through the interview, but writes nothing permanent. When the session ends, those decisions exist only in conversation context. They end up buried in session journals (daily logs, handoff docs) and become hard to find as the project grows.

The real cost surfaces later: when `soul.md`, a `PRD`, or a `harness.md` says something that looks wrong, there's no way to trace *why* that decision was made without reconstructing the session. The rationale is what matters — not just the conclusion — and it's the first thing lost.

items.title: grill-me: no durable output artifact — decisions are lost when session context expires

items.author: Traveller23
items.body:
## Problem
`implement` says to run `/code-review` once the work is done, then commit it.

However, `code-review` reviews `git diff <fixed-point>...HEAD`, which excludes staged and working-tree changes. If `implement` has not already created an interim commit, `/code-review` cannot review the work that is about to be committed.

## Solution
Could you clarify the intended workflow, or update one of the skills so the review covers the final uncommitted diff?
